argument: Research objects should carry persistent identifiers, rich metadata, standardized access mechanisms, interoperable semantics, provenance, and clear reuse conditions. FAIRness concerns machine-actionable discovery and reuse and does not require that all sensitive data be openly downloadable.
boundary: FAIR is distinct from open, free, ethical, secure, or high quality.
Metadata standards differ by domain and can impose costs.
Access restrictions may be necessary for privacy, sovereignty, or intellectual property.
claim: Research objects should carry persistent identifiers, rich metadata, standardized access mechanisms, interoperable semantics, provenance, and clear reuse conditions. FAIRness concerns machine-actionable discovery and reuse and does not require that all sensitive data be openly downloadable.
interpretation: Principia’s paper-free packages can be FAIR through resolvable metadata, schemas, provenance, and explicit access policy without copying source works.

migration_provenance.source_basics: Wilkinson and colleagues published the FAIR Guiding Principles in 2016; funders, repositories, and research infrastructures adopted them widely.

review_attestation.basis: Explicit owner bulk attestation for the repaired Meta-Principles v2 corpus.

scope.basics: Wilkinson and colleagues published the FAIR Guiding Principles in 2016; funders, repositories, and research infrastructures adopted them widely.

questions: Which assumptions and scope restrictions of this Meta-Principle are inherited by the new Principle?
Does the new Principle provide evidence for a specialization, or only a surface analogy?

title: Scientific Data and Workflows Gain Reuse Value When They Are Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable
